# Promo Card

The in-app feature promotion for dashboards: a product eyebrow, a short pitch and one quiet action, beside a framed peek of the feature that runs off the card's edge and dissolves into it.

```tsx
<PromoCard>
  <PromoCardContent>
    <PromoCardEyebrow>
      <BrandMark wordmark={false} />
      Invoicing
    </PromoCardEyebrow>
    <PromoCardTitle>Get paid for exactly what shipped.</PromoCardTitle>
    <PromoCardDescription>
      Turn delivered work into compliant invoices and follow each one until the payment clears.
    </PromoCardDescription>
    <PromoCardActions>
      <Button variant="secondary">Explore</Button>
    </PromoCardActions>
  </PromoCardContent>
  <PromoCardMedia>
    <InvoicePreview />
  </PromoCardMedia>
</PromoCard>
```

## Installation

```bash
# One-time setup (tokens + lib helpers)
npx koalaui-cli init

# Add this component (its dependencies come along)
npx koalaui-cli add promo-card
```

Manual: run `npm install @phosphor-icons/react radix-ui tailwind-variants tailwind-merge`, then copy the source into `components/ui/promo-card/` and adjust the import paths to your project. Components pull `cn` from `lib/utils`, the `tv` wrapper from `lib/tv`, and (for multi-part components) `createContext` from `lib/create-context`.

## Usage

Promo Card is composed from named parts, like [Card](https://koala-ui.vercel.app/docs/components/card.md). The `PromoCard` root owns the surface, the density and the open state; `PromoCardContent` is the copy column and `PromoCardMedia` the peek beside it.

```tsx title="analytics-promo.tsx"
import {
  PromoCard,
  PromoCardContent,
  PromoCardEyebrow,
  PromoCardTitle,
  PromoCardDescription,
  PromoCardActions,
  PromoCardMedia,
} from "@/components/ui/promo-card"
import { Button } from "@/components/ui/button"
import { BrandMark } from "@/components/landing/brand-mark"

export function AnalyticsPromo() {
  return (
    <PromoCard>
      <PromoCardContent>
        <PromoCardEyebrow>
          <BrandMark wordmark={false} />
          Analytics
        </PromoCardEyebrow>
        <PromoCardTitle>Your whole workspace on one screen.</PromoCardTitle>
        <PromoCardDescription>
          Revenue, subscriptions and churn side by side, refreshed every hour.
        </PromoCardDescription>
        <PromoCardActions>
          <Button variant="secondary">Open dashboard</Button>
        </PromoCardActions>
      </PromoCardContent>
      <PromoCardMedia>
        <img src="/analytics.webp" alt="" />
      </PromoCardMedia>
    </PromoCard>
  )
}
```

## Variants

`default` is a contour with no fill, so it sits on whatever ground the dashboard has. `muted` and `brand` are deliberate tints that set a promo apart from the data cards around it, and `elevated` fills and lifts for a promo that floats over a busy page.

```tsx
<PromoCard variant="default">…</PromoCard>
<PromoCard variant="muted">…</PromoCard>
<PromoCard variant="brand">…</PromoCard>
<PromoCard variant="elevated">…</PromoCard>
```

## Media

The peek is a tray with a screen inside it. It starts on the eyebrow’s line, runs off the right and bottom edges, and fades out to the right through a mask, so it dissolves into any theme’s ground. Put live components in it (every example above is built from DS parts) or an `<img>`, which fills the screen from the top-left. On a phone the peek stacks under the copy and holds its own aspect ratio. It is a picture of the product, so it is `aria-hidden` and `inert` by default.

```tsx
<PromoCard>
  <PromoCardContent>…</PromoCardContent>
  <PromoCardMedia>
    <img src="/home/showcase/bento-product.webp" alt="" />
  </PromoCardMedia>
</PromoCard>
```

## Without media

Every part can be left out. Without a `PromoCardMedia` the card collapses to one column and drops its resting height; without an eyebrow the pitch still lands on the same baseline. Two text-only promos fit side by side in a dashboard row.

```tsx
<PromoCard variant="muted">
  <PromoCardContent>
    <PromoCardEyebrow>
      <BrandMark wordmark={false} />
      Scheduling
    </PromoCardEyebrow>
    <PromoCardTitle>Let clients book the gaps in your week.</PromoCardTitle>
    <PromoCardDescription>Share one link, and every booking lands on the right calendar.</PromoCardDescription>
    <PromoCardActions><Button variant="secondary">Explore</Button></PromoCardActions>
  </PromoCardContent>
</PromoCard>

<PromoCard variant="muted">
  <PromoCardContent>
    <PromoCardTitle>Chase late invoices on autopilot.</PromoCardTitle>
    <PromoCardDescription>Pick a trigger, chain the follow-ups, and let the workflow run until it's paid.</PromoCardDescription>
    <PromoCardActions><Button variant="secondary">Explore</Button></PromoCardActions>
  </PromoCardContent>
</PromoCard>
```

## Dismissible

Add a `PromoCardClose` and the card can be dismissed: it fades out with a slight settle, then leaves the tree. The root works uncontrolled out of the box; pass `open` and `onOpenChange` to keep the choice, which is where a dashboard stores “don’t show this again”.

```tsx
const [open, setOpen] = React.useState(true)

<PromoCard open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen} variant="muted">
  <PromoCardClose />
  <PromoCardContent>…</PromoCardContent>
  <PromoCardMedia>…</PromoCardMedia>
</PromoCard>
```

## Density

Density is Koala’s cross-cutting spacing axis (see [Density](https://koala-ui.vercel.app/docs/foundations/density.md)). For Promo Card it tunes the padding, the resting height and the type step. `compact` is the app default; `comfortable` gives an onboarding or empty dashboard more room. The peek re-aligns to the copy at both.

```tsx
<DensityProvider density="compact">
  <PromoCard>…</PromoCard>
</DensityProvider>

<DensityProvider density="comfortable">
  <PromoCard>…</PromoCard>
</DensityProvider>
```

## API reference

`PromoCard` forwards all `div` props and adds `variant` (`default | muted | brand | elevated`), `density` (`compact | comfortable`), `open`, `defaultOpen` and `onOpenChange`. `PromoCardContent`, `PromoCardEyebrow`, `PromoCardTitle` and `PromoCardMedia` forward `div` props. The eyebrow leads with your app’s mark: in Koala that is `<BrandMark wordmark={false} />`; for another product, put its logo `<img>` in `PromoCardIcon`, which forwards `span` props and sizes the image like the BrandMark tile. `PromoCardDescription` forwards `p` props. `PromoCardActions` adds `size` (default `sm`), imposed on the buttons inside. `PromoCardClose` takes Button props and an `aria-label` (default “Dismiss”). Every part accepts `className`, merged last.

## FAQ

### Why does the preview run off the edge instead of sitting inside the card?

Because the crop is the message. A framed screen cut by the card's right and bottom edges reads as a window onto a bigger product; shrinking the whole feature to fit would make it read as a thumbnail. The right edge fades through a CSS mask rather than a painted gradient, so it dissolves into any theme's ground, including the tinted variants.

### Should the preview be a screenshot or live components?

Either works. Live DS parts re-theme with the dashboard, stay sharp at any zoom and cost no image weight, so they're the better default for UI you already ship. Use an image when the feature is visual (a map, a chart you don't render in the DS) or when it isn't built yet. An image fills the screen from its top-left corner.

### Is the preview announced to screen readers?

No. PromoCardMedia is aria-hidden and inert by default, since it's a picture of the product, and nothing inside it can take focus. The title, description and action carry the message. If the preview holds information that isn't in the copy, pass aria-hidden={false} inert={false}.

### Why does the peek move under the copy in a half-width column?

The layout follows the card's own width, not the viewport's. PromoCard is a size container: below 42rem it stacks the peek under the copy, above it puts them side by side. The same promo works in a full dashboard row, a half column and a narrow rail without breakpoints. One consequence: a size container can't take its width from its content, so as a flex item with no width it collapses. Put it in a grid cell or block flow, or give it flex-1 or a width.

### How do I remember that someone dismissed a promo?

Control the card: pass open and onOpenChange, and persist the false you receive (a user setting, a cookie, localStorage). The card plays its exit before it unmounts either way, so the dismissal never pops.

### Why is the action a small secondary button?

A promo points at a feature; it isn't the page's main task. PromoCardActions imposes the sm size, and a secondary button keeps the promo from competing with the dashboard's primary action. Pass size to PromoCardActions or to the Button if you need more weight.

## Exports and dependencies

`npx koalaui-cli add promo-card` writes `components/ui/promo-card/`. Import from `@/components/ui/promo-card`:

- Components and helpers: `PromoCard`, `PromoCardContent`, `PromoCardEyebrow`, `PromoCardIcon`, `PromoCardTitle`, `PromoCardDescription`, `PromoCardActions`, `PromoCardMedia`, `PromoCardClose`, `promoCardVariants`
- Types: `PromoCardProps`, `PromoCardActionsProps`, `PromoCardCloseProps`
- Koala components it installs with it: `button`
- Koala lib helpers it uses: `create-context`, `density`, `tv`
- npm packages: `@phosphor-icons/react`
